purpose: FR-43 part 3: an independent same-draws integration of a low-count integer population coupled to continuous pools. It gives each event's time, channel and the pools at it, for comparison with Cells' integer_unit_population@1 (C3.4, and the two-way case of D315). Declared values and protocol only: no engine value is in this file.

conventions.falling_factorial: ff(n, r) = n!/(n - r)! (ordered tuples; ff(n, 0) = 1, ff(n, r) = 0 for r > n)
conventions.propensity: a_j = k_j * prod_k ff(n_k, r_jk) * phi_j; phi_j = c_read / (1 mM) when channel j declares a read (order 1), else 1; c_read = n / V of the read row at the current continuous state
conventions.total_rate: a0 = sum_j a_j over the channels in declared order
conventions.hazard: H(t) = integral from t_prev to t of a0(x(s), N) ds, with N constant between events; t_prev = 0 before the first event, else the previous event's time (H restarts at 0 after every event)
conventions.threshold: event k (k = 0, 1, 2, ... in order) fires at the first t with H(t) = E_k, E_k = -ln(u1_k)
conventions.channel_rule: at the crossing state: c_j = a_1 + ... + a_j, summed left to right in declared order; the channel is the first j with c_j > min(u2_k * a0, nextafter(a0, 0)), a0 the total at the crossing state
conventions.jump: N <- N - r_j + p_j at the crossing; the continuous state is continuous across it
conventions.draws: u1_k and u2_k are draw k of the site's events stream (README, the random-draw protocol); draws.json holds them as float.hex strings
conventions.stop: events with t_k <= horizon_s; the system is integrated to horizon_s

system.continuous_state: x = (n_cell, n_node): the amounts of species S in the cell and in its finite outside node
system.integer_state: N = (n_free, n_active), the counts of the site's unit states, in that order
system.transfer: J = G * (n_cell / V_cell - n_node / V_node), G = sum_k g_k n_k (only active units conduct here): fmol/s from the cell to the node
system.odes: dn_cell/dt = -J + P_cell; dn_node/dt = +J - k_node * n_node (P_cell and k_node are 0 where a world declares no turnover)
system.between_events: N is constant; only x and H change
system.no_other_motion: S has no other route: no membrane permeability, no face, no reaction; nothing else moves it

worlds.description: FR-43's world: two free subunits form one active unit, which transfers S between the cell and its finite node; the assembly rate reads S in the cell (feedback on); no other writer
Four free subunits (states (4,0), (2,1), (0,2)), so both channels compete at (2,1) and the channel rule draws on u2; feedback on; no other writer

The two-way case: an existing writer (scheduled turnover) produces S in the cell, the pool the assembly clock reads, and clears it at first order at the node; the active count sets the transfer, which changes the later pools and the clearance flux

turnover.law: constant production P in the cell; first-order clearance k n_node at the node; both constant over the horizon

worlds.description: Four free subunits whose assembly reads S at the node (the pool the transfer fills), so the feedback runs the other way; no other writer

draws.generator: make_draws.py (standalone: JAX's random primitives, no engine import)
draws.premise_check: regenerate the draws from README's written rule with your own code and compare with draws.json bit for bit before integrating

requested_outputs.file: one JSON per world, {world, events, samples, method, accuracy}
requested_outputs.events: for each event k with t_k <= horizon_s: k, time_s, channel (id), counts_after {free, active}, cell_S_fmol and node_S_fmol at t_k, transferred_fmol (cumulative cell to node, from t = 0, at t_k), and for W3 turnover_produced_fmol and turnover_cleared_fmol (cumulative, at t_k)
requested_outputs.samples: at each sample time: cell_S_fmol, node_S_fmol, counts {free, active}, transferred_fmol, and for W3 the two turnover totals
requested_outputs.method: the integrator and its tolerances, the event location (root finder and its tolerance) and the second method used as a cross-check
requested_outputs.accuracy: the largest difference between the two methods, per world, in event times (s) and amounts (fmol); target event times to 1e-10 s and amounts to 1e-12 relative
